Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Value=2 (partial) because Comoros’ payments governance includes explicit financial inclusion orientation (National Payment System Strategy; World Bank “Financial Inclusion Project” focusing on payment systems) and multi-stakeholder processes for inclusion strategy development (NFIS workshop including banks, EMIs, telecom operators, and consumer associations), but I did not find evidence of formalized pro-poor representation/mandates within the payment scheme governance itself (e.g., reserved seats for consumer/low-income groups in scheme governance).
